Steps: This document defines test scenarios for the Authentication & Authorization module of RostrLink.
In scope: login
Expected Result: logout

Steps: Out of scope: full CRUD for school domain entities
Expected Result: UI testing
column9: external email infrastructure validation beyond local mail test

Steps: Required services: PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, MailHog, Spring Boot application.
Recommended tools: IntelliJ IDEA run configuration, Postman or IntelliJ HTTP Client, Docker Compose for local infrastructure.
Database and Redis are running; Flyway migrations are applied; test user accounts exist; MailHog is available for OTP email verification.

Title: Login success
Preconditions: User account exists and is active; correct password is known
Steps: Send POST /auth/login with valid identifier and password; include browser/device headers if required
Expected Result: HTTP 200; response contains success envelope; session cookie is set; session is stored in Redis; login response includes user info, roles, and scope

Title: Login failure with wrong password
Preconditions: Active user account exists
Steps: Send POST /auth/login with valid identifier and wrong password
Expected Result: HTTP 401; error code indicates invalid credentials; failed login attempt is recorded; no session cookie is created

Title: Login failure with unknown user
Preconditions: No account exists for the provided email
Steps: Send POST /auth/login with unknown identifier and any password
Expected Result: HTTP 401; error is generic and does not reveal user existence; no session is created

Title: Account lockout after repeated failures
Preconditions: Active user account exists; lockout threshold is configured
Steps: Send repeated login requests with wrong password until threshold is exceeded
Expected Result: User becomes locked; subsequent login attempts return HTTP 403; response indicates account locked; lockout timestamp is set in the database

Title: Login success after unlock period
Preconditions: User account was previously locked; lockout time has expired or account was manually unlocked
Steps: Send POST /auth/login with valid identifier and correct password
Expected Result: HTTP 200; user can log in successfully; session cookie is created again

Title: Logout
Preconditions: User is logged in; session cookie is present
Steps: Send POST /auth/logout
Expected Result: HTTP 200; session is removed from Redis; session cookie is cleared; persistent session record is marked revoked if stored in DB

Title: Access current session info
Preconditions: User is logged in
Steps: Send GET /auth/me
Expected Result: HTTP 200; current session data is returned; user information, roles, and scope are present

Title: Forgot password request
Preconditions: User account exists; MailHog is running
Steps: Send POST /auth/forgot-password with registered email and email channel
Expected Result: HTTP 200; response does not reveal whether account exists; OTP token is created; email is received in MailHog

Title: OTP verification success
Preconditions: OTP was generated for the user; OTP is still valid
Steps: Send POST /auth/verify-otp with email, OTP, and correct purpose
Expected Result: HTTP 200; OTP is marked as used; response indicates verification success

Title: OTP verification failure
Preconditions: OTP exists or test generates one
Steps: Send POST /auth/verify-otp with invalid or expired OTP
Expected Result: HTTP 400; error code indicates invalid OTP; OTP remains unusable

Title: Password reset success
Preconditions: Valid OTP exists for password reset; user account exists
Steps: Send POST /auth/reset-password with email, valid OTP, and new password
Expected Result: HTTP 200; password hash is updated; failed attempt count is reset; lock status is cleared; all existing sessions are revoked

Title: Password reset failure with invalid OTP
Preconditions: User account exists
Steps: Send POST /auth/reset-password with invalid OTP
Expected Result: HTTP 400; password is not changed; no sessions are revoked

Title: Kiosk PIN login success
Preconditions: Kiosk account exists; valid PIN is known
Steps: Send POST /auth/kiosk/pin-login with kiosk ID and correct PIN
Expected Result: HTTP 200; kiosk session is created; kiosk TTL is applied; session cookie is set

Title: Kiosk PIN login failure
Preconditions: Kiosk account exists
Steps: Send POST /auth/kiosk/pin-login with kiosk ID and wrong PIN
Expected Result: HTTP 401; no session is created; failed attempt is recorded

Title: NFC scan login success
Preconditions: NFC tag exists and is active; NFC tag is linked to a user
Steps: Send POST /auth/kiosk/nfc-scan with kiosk ID and valid tag code
Expected Result: HTTP 200; kiosk session is created; returned session is associated with the linked user

Title: NFC scan login failure
Preconditions: NFC tag is revoked or invalid
Steps: Send POST /auth/kiosk/nfc-scan with kiosk ID and invalid tag code
Expected Result: HTTP 401; no session is created

Title: Device fingerprint mismatch
Preconditions: User has an active session; session is bound to a device fingerprint
Steps: Login from device A; reuse same session cookie from device B with different fingerprint headers; access a protected endpoint
Expected Result: HTTP 403; request is rejected; session may remain revoked depending on implementation

Title: Session expiration
Preconditions: A session exists with a short TTL
Steps: Wait until the session expires; send a protected request using the old cookie
Expected Result: HTTP 401; session is treated as expired; access is denied

Title: Rate limit by IP
Preconditions: Rate limit configuration is enabled
Steps: Send many login requests from the same IP within the configured window
Expected Result: HTTP 429; further requests are blocked temporarily; response indicates rate limit exceeded

Title: Validation error handling
Preconditions: Endpoint validation is enabled
Steps: Send malformed or incomplete JSON to a validated endpoint; e.g. missing required email or password
Expected Result: HTTP 400; validation error details are returned; no session or database changes occur

Title: Role loading for active user
Preconditions: User has one or more active roles
Steps: Log in as the user; inspect returned roles
Expected Result: Active roles are returned; scope is loaded correctly; inactive roles are excluded

Title: Context scope loaded for user
Preconditions: User has scoped role data in user_roles
Steps: Log in as the user; inspect scope in response
Expected Result: Scope data is returned; combined scope reflects assigned roles

Title: Permission cache behavior
Preconditions: User has an active role; permission cache is empty
Steps: Log in once; repeat the same protected request
Expected Result: First access loads permissions into cache; second access uses cached permissions; access result remains consistent

Title: Permission change invalidates access
Preconditions: User has an active session; role or permission assignment is changed in the database
Steps: Change role/permission assignment; reuse the existing session; access a protected endpoint
Expected Result: Session is re-evaluated or revoked; access is denied if permissions are outdated

Title: Flyway migration success
Preconditions: Empty database schema
Steps: Start the application
Expected Result: Flyway applies migrations successfully; required tables are created; application starts without schema errors

Title: Redis connectivity
Preconditions: Redis is running
Steps: Start the application; log in a user
Expected Result: Redis session is created successfully; no Redis connection error occurs

Title: MailHog OTP delivery
Preconditions: MailHog is running; registered user exists
Steps: Trigger forgot password; open MailHog UI
Expected Result: OTP email is visible in MailHog; email content contains expected OTP info

Title: Missing cookie on protected endpoint
Preconditions: None
Steps: Call a protected endpoint without session cookie
Expected Result: HTTP 401; authentication required response

Title: Reused revoked session
Preconditions: User logged in; then logged out
Steps: Reuse old cookie on protected endpoint
Expected Result: HTTP 401; session invalid or expired

Title: Expired OTP reuse
Preconditions: OTP exists and is allowed to expire
Steps: Wait for OTP expiry; attempt verify/reset with expired OTP
Expected Result: HTTP 400; OTP rejected

Title: Multiple concurrent sessions
Preconditions: None
Steps: Log in multiple times from different devices; exceed the configured concurrent session limit
Expected Result: Oldest session is revoked or new login is blocked according to policy

Steps: Use Postman collection variables for base URL and test credentials; use MailHog to inspect OTP emails; reset test data between runs if tests modify lockout/session state; start infrastructure before running request tests.
